audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] instructs 'Reflect Demonic Ascension back the moment he commits'. Demonic Ascension is a self-buff transform with a drain aura (kit: 'Swain transforms into a demon and drains health from nearby enemy champions'), not a projectile. Rebuttal cannot reflect it. tldr repeats the claim as 'your reflect makes his best spell a liability'.
audit.why: This is the single most dangerous line in the entry: it tells a Mel player to stand inside Swain's drain radius holding W, expecting a reflect that cannot happen. The only Swain ability carrying the projectile flag is Nevermove (E).
audit.corrected: Rebuttal's reflect target in this matchup is Nevermove (E) — the outgoing wave is the projectile. Against Demonic Ascension the answer is spacing, not W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json (R flags: slow only; E flags: projectile, hardCC, zone)

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and report[3].t all state Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds' after it is spent.
audit.why: Rebuttal's cooldown is 38/35/33/29/26. Twenty seconds is shorter than the ability's cooldown at every single rank, so the player under-rates the cost of burning W on chip. At rank 1 the real hole is 38s — nearly double what the text claims.
audit.corrected: State the real number: W is gone 38s at rank 1, and only reaches 26s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and spikes[2].text both reference a Swain 'Q passive'. Swain has no passive component on Death's Hand.
audit.why: Death's Hand is 'several bolts of eldritch power that pierce through enemies. Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by.' The real mechanic is bolt overlap at close range, which is actionable — spacing wide makes his Q hit for a fraction. 'Q passive' teaches the player to look for something that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Name the real mechanic: Death's Hand stacks damage per bolt, so his poke is only scary at short range.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] attributes Swain's sustain to 'W bomb out-heals your Overwhelm poke'. Vision of Empire (W) does no healing.
audit.why: The sustain chain is: Vision of Empire hitting a champion grants a Soul Fragment; Ravenous Flock (P) is what converts fragments into healing and permanent max health. Getting the source right tells the player what to actually dodge — the W is a fragment generator, and dodging it denies both the heal and the permanent HP.
audit.corrected: Credit the heal to Ravenous Flock and describe W as what feeds it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json (P Ravenous Flock: 'Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health'; W: 'Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Demonic Ascension as the tracked cooldown but gives no number for it or for anything else, and dosFull[2].d is a non-sequitur ('Swain spends Demonic Ascension early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee') sitting under a heading about snaring behind minions.
audit.why: Point 6 asks for the enemy's most punishable cooldown and how long the window really is. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at all ranks and Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 — those two numbers are the whole step-up calculus, and neither appears anywhere in the entry.
audit.corrected: Put the real numbers in: R is 120s flat, Nevermove 12s at rank 1, Vision of Empire 22s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json (R cd 120; E cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10; W cd 22/21/20/19/18)

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and report[0].t open with 'Poke mirror you usually win', while the win rate in the data is 33.33% and the content layer's own level chart hands Swain levels 3 through late.
audit.why: The headline contradicts both the recorded win rate and the entry's own body text. A player reading 'you usually win' will take the extended trades the rest of the entry correctly warns against.
audit.corrected: Reframe as an early-game edge that expires, which is what the body text and the level chart both describe.

audit.why: The missing-interactions file flags needs-antiheal for this matchup, but report Itemization already carries 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', which is the correct call against Ravenous Flock fragments plus R drain. No edit needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on ownership: full.phases marks levels 3-7 as 'Skill' at 5-6/10 with diff 'EVEN', while content.win marks the same levels 'Swain'.
audit.why: Same matchup, two contradictory level charts rendered on one page. Flagging rather than editing — with 6 recorded games I have no basis to pick a new rating, and inventing one would be worse than the disagreement.
audit.corrected: Reported in notes for the user to reconcile; no rating edit proposed.
